purpose: Teach: 證/噺/英和/云わ/ノベル/広東/にたいする/事物

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、旧字「證」、つまり証券の歴史的表記の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your thesis on the historical writing of the character 證—the old form used in securities documents, correct?
lines.style: Measured, genuinely curious. Leaning slightly forward. Warm professional tone—the kind of teacher who's actually read the work. Brief pause before the clarification, giving space for Ren to recognize the thought.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、落語の噺、つまり古典噺の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote my thesis on the history and literary analysis of traditional rakugo storytelling.
lines.style: Quiet correction, not defensive. Direct eye contact. Speaking carefully, as if wanting to be exactly understood. A slight relief that he can clarify what actually matters to him.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、英和辞典の編纂史の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your thesis covered the editorial history of English-Japanese dictionaries, didn't it?
lines.style: Gently probing, thoughtful pause. Testing—not quite challenging, but noticing something. The tone of someone who suspects there's a pattern worth examining.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、古文の云わ、つまり「言わ」の用法研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote my thesis on the usage patterns of the classical verb form 言わ in pre-modern Japanese texts.
lines.style: Steady, grounded response. Speaking with the quiet confidence of someone who knows his own work. No apology in his voice, just factual clarity. The slight firmness of someone used to being misunderstood.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、明治期のノベル、つまり小説の翻訳史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you focused your thesis on the translation history of novels during the Meiji period—is that right?
lines.style: Reflective, almost gentle. The pacing slows slightly. Asuka's tone carries a hint of something—not quite amusement, but the warmth of someone watching a pattern emerge. Inviting him to see it too.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、広東料理の文化史研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—my thesis examined the cultural and historical development of Cantonese cuisine.
lines.style: Calm, straightforward. Speaking without hesitation now. There's an understated dry quality here—Ren answering in a way that suggests he might be aware of what's happening but isn't going to help her along.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦争にたいする世論の歴史研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your thesis dealt with the historical shifts in public opinion regarding war, correct?
lines.style: Slower now, almost gentle. The warmth is still there, but there's a knowing quality—like watching someone realize they've been walking in circles. Asuka's voice carries affection underneath the observation.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、哲学者の事物観の比較研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote my thesis on comparative analysis of how different philosophers conceptualize objects and their nature.
lines.style: Steady and matter-of-fact, closing the pattern without comment. Speaking at his own pace, unruffled. A quiet finality—Ren has answered what was asked, and he's done.
